accuracy.evidence: Matches GCSE Mr from Ar, bracket multipliers (Ca(OH)₂=74), and % by mass (element total/Mr)×100 with CO₂ and H₂SO₄ worked examples.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets counting O₂ once (Mr=28), ignoring bracket subscripts, skipping ×100 in %, and wrong numerators — each in trap step, predictions, challenge why(), and adult notes.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab is Ar summing, bracket expansion and % by mass — distinct from displayed/structural formula drawing (flagformula) and from alkane chain building (flagalkane).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner adds each Ar, expands brackets, computes %, and builds H₂SO₄ before confirmation text.

predictions.evidence: Wrong options (oxygen once; Mr=17; % without ×100) are the slips the next task overturns.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names the 28-trap, calcium-only multiplier, Ar−Mr, and half-H₂SO₄ slips specifically.

readability.evidence: Ages 14–16 GCSE wording: short worked totals, Ar/Mr defined before use, within adult readability limits.

no_filler.evidence: No delve/journey phrasing; each line teaches summing, brackets, or % by mass.

mobile.evidence: Atom and Mr choice buttons remain tappable at 390 px; formula text wraps without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: Each Ar add and Mr choice has a button twin; say() refreshes canvas aria-label; challenge uses aria-live feedback.

sources: AQA GCSE Chemistry: Relative formula mass and percentage by mass calculations
OCR Gateway Chemistry: Calculating Mr from Ar and using brackets in formulae
